text:
Chris B.: Morning — first day on runtime, trying to build from source following the README. cmake passes but linking fails at final link step with libcublas missing. anyone available for a quick sanity check?
```
-- Configuring done
-- Generating done
-- Build files written to: /home/chris/redwood/runtime/build
[100%] Linking CXX executable tests/inference_unit_tests
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcublas
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
I have CUDA 12.1 installed (nvcc --version shows 12.1), Ubuntu 22.04, GCC 11.3.0. I tried `export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.1` and re-run cmake but same error.

Samir: welcome! quick checks: 1) ensure `/usr/local/cuda` symlink points to `cuda-12.1` 2) run `sudo ldconfig` or add `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 3) confirm the dev libs are installed (`libcublas` from the CUDA repo). Run `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so*`

Rosie: also run the helper `scripts/dev/verify_cuda.sh` (we added that to dev docs). if you're on bare metal, check `nvidia-smi` output — driver/toolkit mismatch is a common cause.

Chris B.: `nvidia-smi` shows driver 535.54.03 and GPUs visible. `ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64` shows `libcublas.so.11 -> libcublas.so.11.10.1` but no `libcublas.so` plain symlink. maybe cmake is looking for `-lcublas` and can't resolve?

Eli: CMake should link against SONAME fine, `-lcublas` resolves to the SONAME. If `ld` complains, run `ldconfig` and check `ldconfig -p | grep cublas`. Also try `ldd tests/inference_unit_tests | grep cublas` after a failed link to see what it's trying to pick up.

Samir: if you don't want to mess with host libs, use our dev container: `docker run --gpus=all -it --rm -v $PWD:/work redwood/dev:cuda-12.1 bash` — that image has the CUDA runtime and dev libs installed. If you prefer host, install `libcublas-12-1` from the NVIDIA apt repo.

Rosie: small cmake tip: pass `-DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1` and sometimes `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1` helps find libs.

build-bot: build-bot: FYI CI/dev images are tagged `redwood/runtime-dev:cuda12-2025-02-01` in our registry.

Chris B.: switched to the container from the advice above — `cmake` now completes, but `make -j` fails during link with `undefined reference to cublasCreate_v2`.

Eli: check link order and flags. We usually see this when `-lcublas` is missing or placed after objects that need it. Run `VERBOSE=1 make` to inspect the exact link line. Also ensure the CMake target uses `target_link_libraries(myexe PUBLIC ${CUDA_LIBRARIES})` (or `CUDA::cublas` if using new CMake modules).

Samir: another debug: try a minimal repro: `cat > test.cu <<'EOF'
#include <cublas_v2.h>
int main(){cublasHandle_t h; cublasCreate_v2(&h); return 0;}
EOF
nvcc test.cu -lcublas -o a.out` — if nvcc links & runs, the toolkit is fine and the problem is CMake config.

Chris B.: repro with nvcc links fine inside container, so it's our CMake setup. VERBOSE=1 shows `-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -lcublas` present on the link line though.

Rosie: if nvcc links but CMake doesn't, check if you're accidentally creating a static archive before linking (e.g., building `.a` and then linking without `-Wl,--whole-archive`), or if the target uses `OBJECT` libraries that change link semantics. Also confirm you're not stripping symbols with `-Wl,--as-needed` ordering issues.

Chris B.: good pointers — I'll diff our CMakeLists with the working example in `examples/cmake/cublas_repro` and iterate. thanks for the quick help, this unblocks my day 1. :wave:

Samir: awesome, ping me if you want a screenshare. welcome to runtime team! :tada:
